Hi Jordan,

We started seeing a big uptick in end-to-end RTT for inference calls originating in Frankfurt (eu-central). p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~620ms around 07:50Z and error rate crept up shortly after. This is impacting our feature rollout (sessionization pipeline).

Attached a short capture and a dashboard screenshot. Can you confirm whether this is on your side? We are seeing a strong correlation with requests that are routed to us-west (oddly) — previously they stayed in eu-central.

-Sanjay

- We'll follow up with an interim mitigation within 60–90 minutes and a RCA within 4 business hours.

Adding context from infra:
- Observed a step change in RTT for eu-central clients starting ~07:49Z with a simultaneous BGP next-hop change for a subset of prefixes carrying Skyline traffic.
- A recent peering policy push (INF-2198) rolled out at 07:45Z to enforce new export filters for cost-optimization; preliminary diffs show an accidental deny on eu peer preference for the Skyline AS (AS65109).
- Traffic for those prefixes is currently hairpinned to our us-west POP for ~40% of connections, increasing #hops and RT.

I'm rolling a targeted routing-policy revert for Skyline prefixes now and will monitor p95. Patching notes attached.

Marissa
Sr. Infra Engineer — Routing & Peering
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: routing-policy-diff-20280209.patch (text)

Update: rollback applied at 08:55Z for the affected export filter. Observability shows p95 for Skyline's Frankfurt traffic falling from ~620ms -> ~130ms within two minutes of the rollback. Error rate followed accordingly.

Steps taken:
- Reverted INF-2198 export changes for prefixes: 198.51.100.0/24, 198.51.101.0/24 (Skyline mapping).
- Deployed a short-lived BGP policy that pins Skyline AS to eu peering for the next 24 hours.
- Captured annotated pcap and uploaded to Drive.

Recommended follow-ups (for RCA):
- Postmortem to review rollout gating and canarying of peering changes.
- Add a pre-flight check to validate AS-specific export preferences.

Subject: Re: sudden latency spikes — production impact

Sanjay / Elena — following up with a summary and next steps. Thanks for your patience.

What happened (short):
- During a peering policy rollout we unintentionally weakened eu peering preference for Skyline's prefixes which caused a subset of Frankfurt-originating requests to route via our us-west POP. That increased RTT and transient errors.

What we did (fix):
- Reverted the faulty export filter at 08:55Z and applied a temporary eu-pin policy for Skyline. Observed p95 return to baseline within minutes.

Customer ask / next steps:
- We will run a full RCA and postmortem (shared doc link above) and implement a preflight validation for AS-specific export preferences before future peering rollouts.
- As an immediate customer gesture, Sean will reach out about a one-off service credit; Jordan will coordinate timelines for a joint postmortem.

You're in our priority queue for the next 24 hours; please ping me directly if you see any regression.

— Jordan
